what: e.l.f. Beauty sells cosmetics at low prices. Its model is to identify what is selling at premium price points, develop a close equivalent quickly, and sell it for a fraction of the price through mass retailers and its own website. It also owns Naturium, Keys Soulcare and the Rhode skincare brand.
customers: Younger consumers, largely reached through social media rather than traditional advertising, buying at Target, Walmart, Ulta and online.
money: Face, eye and lip products under the e.l.f. brand at mass price points.
e.l.f. SKIN, Naturium, Keys Soulcare and Rhode.
moat: Speed and marketing efficiency. e.l.f. can bring a product from concept to shelf far faster than legacy cosmetics companies, and it reaches its customers through social media at a fraction of the cost of television advertising. That combination lets it hold low prices while funding growth, and retailers give it more shelf space each year because it turns over fast.
risks: The shares trade at about 76 times earnings, which allows no room for a slowdown.
Net income of only $86.6M on $1.9B of revenue shows how much is being spent on marketing and on integrating acquisitions.
The Rhode acquisition was expensive, and debt has risen to $916.9M against $289.7M of cash.
Growth has slowed from its extraordinary pace, and in a trend-driven category a few quarters of weaker product can change the trajectory quickly.
Tariffs on goods manufactured in China raise cost directly, and the low price points leave little room to absorb that.
opportunities: Revenue has grown extraordinarily, from $392.2M in 2022 to $1.6B in 2026, with trailing revenue of about $1.9B.
Free cash flow of $275.7M is far above net income, which means the reported earnings understate the cash the business produces.
Rhode brings a genuinely premium brand with a strong following, which diversifies away from value-priced colour cosmetics.
International markets are still small for e.l.f. relative to the US, and the model travels well.
Sixteen analysts average a $131.00 target, about 20% above the current price.
watch: Market share in US mass cosmetics. e.l.f. has grown by taking share from legacy brands; the moment that share stops rising, a 76 times earnings multiple becomes very hard to defend.
